pool.text: On May 17, Ville-Marie was founded on the southern shore with Maisonneuve as governor.
The wooded mountain park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted was officially inaugurated.
The Canadian Pacific Railway was founded here.
The Mount Royal Cemetery Company established the very first crematorium in Canada.
HEC Montreal was founded, adding an important educational institution to the city.
Montreal-based CN was formed by the Canadian government following bankruptcies.
The Montreal Metro was inaugurated and features many stations.
Saint Joseph's Oratory was completed, joining the city's notable architectural landmarks.
Montreal hosted the International and Universal Exposition, also widely known as Expo 67.
Concordia University was created from the merger of Sir George Williams University and Loyola College.
Montreal hosted the Summer Olympics as the only Canadian city to achieve this.
Montreal Mayor Jean Drapeau brought the Summer Olympic Games to the city.
All passenger services for The Canadian were transferred to Via.
The tragic École Polytechnique massacre took place, becoming one of Canada's worst mass shootings.
The Canadian has terminated in Toronto instead of in Montreal.
The video game industry boomed with the opening of Ubisoft Montreal.
Corporate headquarters of the railway moved to Calgary, Alberta.
Montreal was merged with 27 surrounding municipalities on the Island of Montreal.
BIXI was first launched with Montreal-based PBSC Urban Solutions ICONIC bikes.
The Canadian census reported the city's population at 1,762,949 residents.
